Terminal.Title: Night City Market
Terminal.WaitingForTick: The market opens with the next tick.
Terminal.EmptyGM: No companies yet. Open the Market GM Console to import the starter corporations or create your own.

Portfolio.PrivateHint: Stakes in businesses that are not on the market, valued at book value times your share. They count toward the total but cannot be bought or sold here; click one to open it in the Business window.
Portfolio.ReinvestHint: Use dividends from this holding to buy more shares automatically.
Portfolio.NoPositions: No holdings yet. Open a company on the Market tab to buy shares.
Portfolio.NoGM: No GM is online. Your requests are saved and will be handled when one connects.

Trade.Title: Place order
Trade.SettleNote: Sale proceeds take {n} day(s) to reach your balance. Until then they count towards your total value but cannot be spent or withdrawn.
Trade.BrokerNote: Your broker fills this in about {days} day(s). Lower fees than a direct trade.
Trade.NoBroker: You have no broker. Choose one on the Portfolio tab to trade this way.
Trade.DirectNote: Fills immediately at the highest fees.
Trade.DirectLocked: Direct trading needs a CorpNet terminal session. Connect from the Portfolio tab first.
Trade.Hint: Market orders fill at the price when they execute, which may differ from the quote shown. Limit and stop orders need a price.

Fund.Title: Funds
Fund.Name: Fund
Fund.NavNote: Unit value follows the companies the fund holds.
Fund.BrokerOnly: Funds can only be bought and sold through a broker, and only at market.

Alerts.Title: Price alerts
Alerts.Hint: Get told when a stock or fund passes a price, or moves a lot in one day. Alerts are checked after each market tick.
Alerts.ValueHint: A price in eb, or for a daily move a percentage (0.5 to 50)

Line.move: {ticker} moves {value}% or more in a day

Statement.Hint: Mailed by your broker, or by the market wire if you have none. Turn on monthly statements under Notifications.

FundEditor.Title: Fund
FundEditor.Rebalance: Rebalance back to its starting mix
FundEditor.DistributionHint: An accumulating fund adds its holdings' dividends to its unit value. A distributing one sets them aside and pays holders cash each month or quarter (or reinvests it for those who switch reinvestment on). A redemption delay holds sellers' money for that many days after they sell.
FundEditor.RebalanceHint: Rebalancing resets the holdings to the mix the fund had when it was created or last edited, so winners do not take over. The manager's edge adds (or, if negative, subtracts) that much a year on top of what the holdings earn. Use it for an actively managed fund.
FundEditor.ComponentsHint: One company per line: ticker and weight, for example ARA 30. Weights are shared out in proportion.

Access.Title: Trading access
Access.ChooseBroker: Choose a broker to trade funds and to place cheaper, slower orders.
Access.NoBrokersExist: No brokers are available yet. Ask your GM.
Access.Stocks: Stocks only, market or limit orders
Access.FundEdge: Fund entry and exit charges waived
Access.MailHint: You can also mail your broker: BUY 10 ARA, SELL 5 MIL, WITHDRAW 5000, STATUS, CANCEL and an order reference.
Access.WithdrawViaBroker: Your broker handles withdrawals. They are slower and arrive as eddies by mail.
Access.WithdrawDirect: With no broker, withdrawals go straight to your wallet. A broker makes them slower but cheaper.
Access.GrantedByGM: Your GM has granted you terminal access.
Access.OnNetwork: This device is on the CorpNet network.
Access.NeedsCorpnet: You need a terminal connected to the CorpNet network.
Access.OpenMode: Direct trading is open to everyone. No terminal session is needed.

ApproachHint.careful: DV −2, three quarters of the effect.
ApproachHint.standard: The DV and the effect as they are.
ApproachHint.bold: DV +3, a quarter more effect, and some risk later.

Roll.Title: Roll
Roll.UseBonus: Use the +1 a partner's check left for this
Roll.UseExtra: Take extra time: spend one of this week's business days for +1
Roll.Needed: Needs {n} or more on the d10.
Roll.NeededCrit: Needs a 10 on the d10, and then a good second die.
Roll.Hint: A 10 adds a second d10 and a 1 takes one away, as usual. Luck is spent from your sheet when you roll, whatever happens. Nothing is rolled until you press Roll.
Roll.NothingToRoll: There is nothing this character can roll for that.
Roll.HireNote: A hired professional's fixed base replaces your stat and skill. Their fee is paid from the business even if the roll fails, and Luck cannot be spent on their roll.

plan.fumble: A muddled plan: Reputation starts 8 lower.
plan.failure: A weak plan: Reputation starts 5 lower.
plan.narrow: A workable plan: Reputation carries on as it is.
plan.solid: A good plan: Reputation starts 3 higher.
plan.strong: A strong plan: Reputation starts 5 higher.
plan.exceptional: A plan investors love: Reputation starts 8 higher.

registration.narrow: Registered: Compliance carries on as it is.
registration.exceptional: Filed without a query: Compliance starts 8 higher.

capital.fumble: Refused, and the books are a mess: try again in 14 days.
capital.failure: Refused: the fee is spent; try again in 7 days.
capital.narrow: Passed narrowly: the capital quote is near the top of the range.
capital.strong: Passed well: a low capital quote.
capital.exceptional: Passed brilliantly: the lowest capital quote.

setupRoll.fumble: The setup falls through: half the lowest setup cost is lost (never more than half the money put in), and you can try again in 14 days.
setupRoll.failure: The setup falls through: a third of the lowest setup cost is lost (never more than half the money put in), and you can try again in 7 days.
setupRoll.narrow: It opens, but the setup costs close to the top of the range, at 85% Capacity.
setupRoll.solid: It opens at a fair setup cost, at full Capacity.
setupRoll.strong: It opens cheaply, with 10% more Capacity.
setupRoll.exceptional: It opens at the lowest setup cost, with 20% more Capacity.

assist.narrow: +1 to this week's roll for the action.
assist.solid: +1 to this week's roll for the action.
assist.strong: +1 to this week's roll for the action.
assist.exceptional: +1 to this week's roll for the action.

work.fumble: A bad week: takings down by about 40%.

promote.fumble: The word on the street turns against you: Reputation down.

source.fumble: A bad deal: the Cost base goes up.
source.narrow: The Cost base down a little.
source.exceptional: The Cost base down a lot.

respond.fumble: It goes badly: 20% of the week's takings lost, and the full mark.
respond.failure: It falls short: 10% of the week's takings lost, and half the mark.

loanRoll.fumble: Refused, and you will not be welcome back for 14 days.
loanRoll.failure: Refused; you can ask again in 14 days.
loanRoll.narrow: Up to 6 weeks of average profit, at 1.5% a week.
loanRoll.solid: Up to 10 weeks of average profit, at 1.2% a week.
loanRoll.strong: Up to 14 weeks of average profit, at 1% a week.
loanRoll.exceptional: Up to 20 weeks of average profit, at 0.8% a week.

angelRoll.fumble: The angel walks away; another will listen in 14 days.
angelRoll.failure: The angel walks away; another will listen in 14 days.
angelRoll.narrow: 20% of the book value, at 10% under book.
angelRoll.solid: 30% of the book value, at book.
angelRoll.strong: 40% of the book value, at 10% over book.
angelRoll.exceptional: 50% of the book value, at 20% over book.

stepUpRoll.fumble: Refused, and the paperwork is a mess: the fee is spent and you can try again in 14 days.
stepUpRoll.failure: Refused: the fee is spent and you can try again in 7 days.
stepUpRoll.narrow: Registered, but the inspectors will be watching: Compliance starts at 45.
stepUpRoll.strong: Registered with clean books: Compliance starts at 55.
stepUpRoll.exceptional: Registered without a single query: Compliance starts at 60.

keepSafe.fumble: It goes badly: half as much protection money again this week.
keepSafe.narrow: A quarter off this week's protection money.
keepSafe.solid: Half off this week's protection money.
keepSafe.strong: Three quarters off this week's protection money.

Accepted.Subject: Order {ref} received
Accepted.Line2: Expect it to complete in about {days}.
Accepted.Line3: Reference {ref}. Mail CANCEL {ref} to withdraw it.

Filled.Subject: Order {ref} filled
Filled.TimingBetter: I got you {bps} basis points better than the quoted value.
Filled.TimingWorse: The timing went {bps} basis points against you.
Filled.Settles: The money reaches your balance in {days}.

WithdrawalQueued.Subject: Withdrawal {ref} received
WithdrawalQueued.Line1: I am pulling {amount} eb from your account. My fee is {fee} eb.
WithdrawalQueued.Line2: Expect the money in about {days}. Reference {ref}.

WithdrawalPaid.Subject: Your {amount} eb
WithdrawalPaid.Line1: Here is your {amount} eb. Claim it from this message.

WithdrawalFailed.Subject: Withdrawal could not be paid
WithdrawalFailed.Line1: I could not deliver your withdrawal. {amount} eb is back in your account.

Cancelled.Subject: Cancelled: {ref}
Cancelled.withdrawal: Withdrawal {ref} is cancelled and the money is back in your account.

Help.Subject: What I can do
Help.Line1: Mail me an order, one command per line.
Help.Commands: BUY 10 ARA / SELL 5 MIL / SELL ALL ARA / SELL 5 MIL @ 80 / WITHDRAW 5000 / STATUS / STATEMENT / CANCEL ref / HELP
Help.Line2: I work at my own pace, so allow a few days.

NotClient.Subject: We do not work together
NotClient.Line1: You have not hired me. Choose a broker in your portfolio first.

Status.Subject: Your account
Status.Line1: Balance {cash} eb, holdings {holdings} eb, {orders} open order(s).

Movers.Subject: Big movers in your holdings
Movers.Line1: These holdings moved {pct}% or more today:
Movers.Mover: {ticker} {pct} to {price} eb ({delta} eb on your position)

Up.1: I'm hearing good things behind the scenes at {name} ({ticker}). Something has gone their way, and it may not be in the price yet.
Up.2: There's a good story going round about {name}. Nothing official, but the people who know {ticker} are in a better mood than usual.
Up.3: A contact close to {name} sounded pleased with themselves this week. I'd keep an eye on {ticker}.
Up.4: Chatter on the desks says {name} has had a win it hasn't announced. {ticker} may not have caught up yet.
Up.5: Somebody who should know says {ticker} is on firmer ground than the price suggests.
Up.6: I've heard {name} did something right, and the market hasn't noticed. Not for long, I'd guess.
Up.7: The mood around {name} has turned. Quietly, and for the better. Worth knowing if you hold {ticker}.
Up.8: There's a smile going round the {ticker} crowd. I can't tell you why, only that it's a good one.

Down.1: I'm hearing bad things behind the scenes at {name} ({ticker}). Something has gone wrong for them, and it may not be in the price yet.
Down.2: There's an ugly story going round about {name}. Nothing official, but the people who know {ticker} are quieter than usual.
Down.3: A contact close to {name} sounded rattled this week. I'd keep an eye on {ticker}.
Down.4: Chatter on the desks says {name} has had a setback it hasn't announced. {ticker} may not have caught up yet.
Down.5: Somebody who should know says {ticker} is on shakier ground than the price suggests.
Down.6: I've heard {name} got something badly wrong, and the market hasn't noticed. Not for long, I'd guess.
Down.7: The mood around {name} has turned. Quietly, and for the worse. Worth knowing if you hold {ticker}.
Down.8: There's a long face going round the {ticker} crowd. I can't tell you why, only that it's a bad one.

Hedge.1: Rumours only, and I never said it. It can take a few days to show, if it shows at all.
Hedge.2: Take it with a pinch of salt. These things are right more often than they should be, and wrong just often enough to hurt.
Hedge.3: I can't prove any of it. Do what you like with it.
Hedge.4: It might be nothing. It might take a week to matter. Watch the price.
Hedge.5: You didn't hear this from me.
Hedge.6: Nothing is certain until it's in the price, and by then it's too late to care.

WarningLine.1: Some of your recent trades have lined up very neatly with news that came out afterwards. I am not accusing anyone, but people in my line of work notice that sort of thing.
WarningLine.2: I have been hearing questions about the timing of certain trades, and some of them are yours.
WarningLine.3: Your account has been looked at. Nothing official, but looked at, and I would rather you heard it from me.
WarningLine.4: There is talk about how well your trades have been timed around corporate news. Talk like that has a way of becoming more than talk.

WarningAdvice.1: If I were you I would trade less around company news for a while.
WarningAdvice.2: Keep your head down for a bit and let it blow over.
WarningAdvice.3: I would think hard before you do that again.

EnquirySubject.2: NCPD Financial Crimes: a few questions

EnquiryLine.1: NCPD Financial Crimes is carrying out a routine review of trading activity around a number of recent corporate announcements. Your account has come up. No action is being taken at this time.
EnquiryLine.2: This is a courtesy notice. Trades on your account have been flagged for review as part of an ordinary enquiry into the timing of trades around company news.
EnquiryLine.3: Your recent trading has been selected for a routine compliance review. You are not required to respond, and no finding has been made.

EnquiryAdvice.1: We would remind you that trading on information not available to the public is an offence.
EnquiryAdvice.2: Further activity of this kind may result in a formal investigation.

Fine.Subject: Notice of penalty
Fine.Line1: Following a review of your trading around recent corporate announcements, a penalty of {amount} eb has been taken from your brokerage balance.
Fine.Short: Your balance did not cover it. {amount} eb remains unpaid and has been noted against your name.
Fine.Line2: This notice is final. Further activity of this kind will be referred for prosecution.

Freeze.Subject: Account restriction
Freeze.Line1: Your brokerage account has been frozen for {days} while we complete a review of your trading. You cannot place orders or withdraw funds in that time. Open orders have been voided.
Freeze.Line2: You may still pay money in. The restriction will lift on its own.

Dropped.Subject: Our arrangement
Dropped.Line1: Your broker can no longer act for you. Any orders still open through them have been cancelled.
Dropped.Line2: You are free to choose another broker, though this one will not take you back for some time.

Alert.Subject: Price alert: {ticker}
Alert.Above: {name} ({ticker}) has risen to {price} eb, past your alert price of {value} eb.
Alert.Below: {name} ({ticker}) has fallen to {price} eb, past your alert price of {value} eb.
Alert.Move: {name} ({ticker}) moved {pct} today, to {price} eb. You asked to hear about moves of {value}% or more.

Statement.Subject: Brokerage statement, day {to}
Statement.PeriodAll: Covers everything since the account opened, to day {to}.
Statement.Value: Account value now: {total} eb ({cash} eb cash and {holdings} eb in holdings).
Statement.Settling: Of that, {amount} eb is sale proceeds still settling.
Statement.Flows: Paid in {deposits} eb and out {withdrawals} eb. Bought {bought} eb, sold {sold} eb, fees {fees} eb.
Statement.Income: Dividends received: {dividends} eb ({reinvested} eb of it reinvested).
Statement.Performance: Performance after deposits and withdrawals: {gain} eb ({pct}).
Statement.Realized: Realised profit this period: {realized} eb. Unrealised on current holdings: {unrealized} eb.
Statement.Position: {ticker}: {qty} units at {price} eb, worth {value} eb ({weight} of holdings), {pnl} eb ({pnlpct}).

Ledger.syndicatePayout: Paid out by a dissolved syndicate
Ledger.memberRedeem: Paid to a member who redeemed
Ledger.memberPayout: Paid out to a member on dissolving

Reasons.invalid-amount: Enter a whole number of eb, 1 or more.
Reasons.insufficient-wealth: You do not have that much eb in your wallet.
Reasons.below-fee: The amount does not cover the fee.
Reasons.insufficient-balance: Your brokerage balance is too low.
Reasons.invalid-order: That order type is not valid.
Reasons.invalid-qty: Enter a whole number of shares, 1 or more.
Reasons.invalid-limit: Enter a limit or stop price above zero.
Reasons.halted: Trading in that company is halted.
Reasons.insufficient-funds: Not enough uncommitted funds in your brokerage balance.
Reasons.insufficient-shares: You do not hold enough free shares.
Reasons.not-found: That order is no longer open.
Reasons.below-minimum: The order is below the minimum size.
Reasons.invalid-route: Choose a broker or a direct trade.
Reasons.no-terminal-session: Direct trading needs an open CorpNet terminal session.
Reasons.no-broker: You have no broker. Pick one on the Portfolio tab.
Reasons.fund-needs-broker: Funds can only be traded through a broker.
Reasons.locked-out: The terminal has locked you out after a failed attempt. Try again later.
Reasons.no-terminal: The terminal check could not be run. Ask the GM.
Reasons.no-network: This device is not connected to the CorpNet network.
Reasons.not-authenticated: You are connected to CorpNet but not signed in.
Reasons.not-required: Direct trading is open. No terminal session is needed.
Reasons.unrecognised: I did not understand that request.
Reasons.ipo-closed: That offer is not open for subscriptions.
Reasons.ipo-already: You have already subscribed. Cancel that subscription first to change it.
Reasons.ipo-no-allocation: The offer was oversubscribed and your share rounded to nothing.
Reasons.invalid-alert: Enter a price above zero, or for a daily move a percentage from 0.5 to 50.
Reasons.alert-already-met: That price has already been reached. Choose one beyond the current price.
Reasons.too-many-alerts: You have too many alerts. Remove one first.
Reasons.account-frozen: Your account is frozen. It will lift by itself.
Reasons.broker-refuses: That broker will not take you on again just yet.
Reasons.on-cooldown: You tried that too recently. Give it a few days.
Reasons.unknown-action: That is not something you can do.
Reasons.no-check: No roll came with that request. Press the button again to roll.
Reasons.no-roll: No roll came with that request. Press Connect again to roll.
Reasons.roll-missing: The roll could not be found in chat. Roll again.
Reasons.roll-mismatch: That roll was not made by you for this check. Roll again.
Reasons.roll-stale: That roll is too old. Roll again.
Reasons.roll-used: That roll has already been used. Roll again.
Reasons.roll-invalid: That roll could not be read. Roll again.
Reasons.roll-unverified: That roll could not be confirmed. Try again.

Notify.QueuedNoGM: No GM is online. Your request is saved and will run when one connects.
Notify.BrokerCleared: You no longer have a broker.
Notify.SessionEnded: You left CorpNet, so your direct-trading session has ended. Connect to the terminal again to trade directly.
Notify.SessionAlready: Your terminal session is already open.
Notify.SessionOpen: Terminal session open. Accounting check {total} against DV {dv}.
Notify.SessionFailed: Terminal check failed: {total} against DV {dv}. You are locked out for now.
Notify.OrderSentToBroker: Order sent to your broker. Expect it in about {days}.
Notify.WithdrawalQueued: Withdrawal of {amount} eb queued with your broker. Expect it in about {days}.
Notify.WithdrawalCancelled: Withdrawal cancelled and returned to your balance.
Notify.IpoSubscribed: Subscription received. {amount} is held until the company lists.
Notify.StatementRequested: Statement requested. It will arrive by mail.
Notify.Title: Notifications
Notify.MoverPct: Count a holding as a big mover at (% a day)
Notify.Hint: Choose how you hear about market activity. Mail arrives in Night City Messenger. Withdrawals paid through a broker are always mailed, because they carry the money.

Category.tips: Rumours about companies you hold or watch

Errors.NotActiveGM: Only the active GM can run the market. Another GM is currently the active one.
Errors.gm-only: Only a GM can do that.
Errors.ticker-invalid: The ticker needs at least 2 letters or digits.
Errors.price-invalid: The initial price must be at least 1 eb.
Errors.ticker-taken: That ticker is already used by another company or fund.
Errors.components-invalid: A fund needs at least one holding, written like ARA 30.
Errors.components-unknown: Some holdings are not companies on this market.
Errors.not-active-gm: Only the active GM can do that.
Errors.NoActor: No character is available. Ask your GM to assign you a character.
Errors.OutboxFull: You have too many requests waiting. Wait for the GM to process them.

GMConsole.Title: Market GM Console
GMConsole.CalendarAhead: Hand advances have taken the market {days} day(s) past the calendar ({calendar}). Dividends, fund distributions, IPOs and statements fall due on the market date.
GMConsole.CalendarManual: In manual mode the market date moves only when you advance the market; the calendar shows {calendar}. Dividends, fund distributions, IPOs and statements fall due on the market date.
GMConsole.AdvanceDayHint: Move game time on by one whole day in a single step. Delays, sentiment changes and heat windows count it as a day. In the in-world clock mode a tick is only a few minutes of one.
GMConsole.InvalidDays: Enter a whole number of ticks, 1 or more.
GMConsole.ResetConfirm: This erases all prices and history and starts every company again from its initial price. Player portfolios are not affected. Continue?
GMConsole.DeleteConfirm: Delete {name}? Its journal is removed and the company leaves the market.
GMConsole.ActionFailed: That did not work. Check the values and that you are the active GM.
GMConsole.FundsHint: Funds pool several companies into one tradable unit. Their value follows the companies' prices. Players can only trade them through a broker.
GMConsole.CloseFundConfirm: Close {name}? Every holder is paid the current value in cash and the fund is removed.
GMConsole.DirectTermsHint: Direct trades fill at once and cost {commission} plus {flatFee} eb, from a CorpNet terminal after an Accounting check at DV {dv} (network: {network}). Brokers are always slower and cheaper. Change these in module settings.
GMConsole.BrokersHint: A broker's speed and fees come from their Accounting skill (INT plus level) on their character sheet. A contact with no sheet uses the rating set here.
GMConsole.RemoveBrokerHint: Remove this broker from the market. Their character and Night City Messenger contact are not changed. Only possible when no character is using them.
GMConsole.RemoveBrokerConfirm: Remove {name} as a broker? Their character and Night City Messenger contact stay exactly as they are, and you can make them a broker again later.

RemoveBrokerRefused.assigned: Cannot remove this broker while characters use them: {names}. They must choose another broker first.
RemoveBrokerRefused.busy: Cannot remove this broker yet: {names} still have orders or a withdrawal with them. Wait for those to finish.
RemoveBrokerRefused.unknown: That broker is no longer there.
RemoveBrokerRefused.gm-only: Only a GM can do that.

GMConsole.NoBrokers: No brokers yet. Make a character or contact a broker to let players hire them.
GMConsole.TerminalGrantsHint: Characters on a CorpNet-connected device can open a trading session. Grant access here for a terminal that is not on the network.
GMConsole.UndoHint: Step the market back one tick. Not possible once a player's money has moved because of that tick, or after a split, price change or new company.
GMConsole.UndoDone: The market is back at tick {tick}. Advancing again re-runs the tick, with the same random numbers unless you change the controls first.

Undo.not-active-gm: Only the active GM can undo a tick.
Undo.nothing-to-undo: There is no tick to undo.
Undo.settled: Players' money has already moved because of that tick (a fill, a dividend or a paid withdrawal), so it cannot be undone.

Editor.Title: Company
Editor.Name: Name
Editor.AliasesHint: Comma-separated. Other names this company goes by, such as the client name on a gig.
Editor.LoreHint: Plain text. Blank lines start a new paragraph. Edit the journal itself for rich formatting.

News.Dividend: {name} declares a dividend of {amount} eb per share.
News.SpecialDividend: {name} announces a special dividend of {amount} eb per share.
News.Buyout: {name} is acquired. Shareholders are paid {price} eb per share.
News.Delist: {name} is delisted. Shareholders are paid {price} eb per share.
News.Bankrupt: {name} files for bankruptcy. Shares are now worthless.
News.HaltAll: Trading is halted across the market.
News.FundClosed: {name} is closed. Unit holders are paid {price} eb per unit.
News.FundDistribution: {name} pays a distribution of {amount} eb per unit.
News.Ipo: {name} ({ticker}) goes public today at {price} eb per share.
News.IpoOversubscribed: The {name} offer was oversubscribed. Each subscription was filled at {pct}%.

Controls.SentimentHint: A bias nudges prices up or down each day for a while, in units of each stock's normal daily swing. Strength is -3 to 3. Try 0.5 for a gentle push.
Controls.ShockHint: A one-off shock. The price eases toward the new level after the delay, then partly settles back. Use the percentage the price should move by.
Controls.Headline: Public headline (optional)
Controls.HeadlineHint: Shown to players in the News tab
Controls.SetPriceHint: A blunt tool: the price changes at once and is logged. Moving fair value too stops the market pulling the price straight back.

Actions.SpecialDividendHint: Pays every holder now, once. Shares bought today do not qualify.
Actions.SplitHint: An N-for-1 split: holders get N times the shares, the price divides by N, and cost per share adjusts. Charts stay continuous.
Actions.SplitConfirm: Split {name} {ratio}-for-1? Every holder's shares and open orders are adjusted.
Actions.BuyoutHint: The company is acquired. Holders are paid in cash at this price and the stock is retired.
Actions.BuyoutConfirm: Buy out {name} at {price} eb per share? Holders are paid and open orders are cancelled.
Actions.EndHint: Delisting pays holders the last price. Bankruptcy pays nothing and records the loss.
Actions.DelistConfirm: Delist {name}? Holders are paid its last price in cash.
Actions.BankruptConfirm: Declare {name} bankrupt? Every holder loses their position with no payout.

Gig.Title: Gig outcomes
Gig.Intro: When a gig is completed or failed in Night City Map, the bridge sends the result here. The client is matched to a company and its share price reacts after a short delay: a success helps a little, a failure hurts more, and a bigger reward moves it further.
Gig.BridgeMissing: The Night City Map bridge module is not active, so gigs will not arrive by themselves. You can still report an outcome by hand below.
Gig.ApprovalOn: Impacts wait for your approval. Change this in module settings.
Gig.ApprovalOff: Impacts are applied automatically once the client is matched.
Gig.NeedsMappingHint: These clients could not be matched to a company. Pick one, or ignore the client. The choice is remembered for later gigs from the same client.
Gig.NoMapping: Nothing is waiting for a company.
Gig.ReviewHint: Change the size, the delay or the headline if you like, then approve. The headline is published when the price starts to move.
Gig.MappingsHint: A saved mapping always wins over name matching. You can also tag a gig's notes with [NCI: ARA] to name its company, or [NCI: ignore] to skip it.
Gig.ReportHint: For gigs that were not run through the map. Leave the company blank to find it from the client name.

Reason.fuzzy: Close spelling only: check it is the right company
Reason.mention: The company is named in the gig text, not as the client
Reason.tag: Skipped by a tag in the gig notes

Notice.Review: A gig {outcome} for {client} ({name}) is waiting for your approval in the Gigs tab.
Notice.Mapping: A gig for "{client}" needs a company. Open the Gigs tab to choose one.
Notice.Business: A gig {outcome} for {client} is for the players' business {name}. It is waiting for your approval in the Gigs tab.

Gig.Weaker: (weaker: {n} earlier gig(s) for it this month)
Gig.BusinessHint: Gigs whose client is a business the players own change that business, not a share price: its Reputation at once and next week's takings. Each gig for the same business within four weeks counts for less than the one before.

Result.applied: Impact queued. It shows in about {days} day(s).
Result.unmatched: The client was not recognised. Pick a company for it.
Result.disabled: Gig outcomes are switched off in settings.
Result.invalid: Enter an outcome and a client or company.
Result.not-gm: Only the active GM can do that.

mild.1: {name} shares edge up on talk of a quiet win.
mild.2: {name} ticks higher as traders note a good run.
mild.3: Steady buying in {name} after a smooth stretch.
mild.6: Traders nudge {name} higher on encouraging chatter.
mild.7: {name} firms up after a calm, productive spell.
mild.8: A little more confidence in {name} today.

strong.1: {name} jumps as the market warms to its recent run.
strong.2: Strong demand lifts {name} after a very good spell.
strong.3: {name} rallies, with traders pointing to a clear win.
strong.4: {name} surges on word of a standout result.
strong.5: Buyers pile into {name} after a very strong spell.
strong.6: {name} leaps as the street reconsiders its prospects.
strong.7: A burst of optimism sends {name} climbing.
strong.8: {name} takes off, and the desks are scrambling to keep up.

mild.1: {name} slips amid whispers of a setback.
mild.2: {name} drifts lower as traders weigh a rough patch.
mild.3: Light selling in {name} after a messy stretch.
mild.5: A little selling pressure on {name} after an awkward stretch.
mild.7: {name} eases back after an uneven spell.
mild.8: A shade less confidence in {name} today.

strong.1: {name} falls sharply as bad news spreads.
strong.2: Heavy selling hits {name} after a damaging spell.
strong.3: {name} sinks as the market punishes a clear failure.
strong.4: {name} tumbles on word of a serious misstep.
strong.5: Sellers pile out of {name} after a damaging spell.
strong.6: {name} lurches lower as the street reconsiders its prospects.
strong.7: A wave of pessimism sends {name} sliding.
strong.8: {name} drops hard, and the desks are scrambling to keep up.

Heat.Title: Insider-trading heat
Heat.Intro: A gig outcome is private until its price effect starts to show. A character who buys the client before good news, or sells before bad news, in that gap draws heat. Heat is hidden from players, runs from 0 to 100, and halves about every week.
Heat.Off: Heat tracking is switched off in module settings, so nothing is being recorded.
Heat.PhaseNote: Players are warned as heat builds: a nervous word from their broker, then a routine enquiry from NCPD Financial Crimes. At the top a penalty is chosen: a fine, a frozen account, or a broker who walks away. Anything that costs a player something waits here for you, unless you turn approval off in settings.
Heat.SetHeatHint: Set this character's heat directly. Zero clears it.
Heat.PenaltiesHint: What an investigation found. Change the amount or length if you like, then approve; dismiss to let it go. Approving carries it out at once and tells the player.
Heat.BanDays: Days it will not take them back

Penalty.dropBroker: Their broker walks away, and will not take them back for {days} days

Result.not-gm: Only the active GM can do that.

Notice.Pending: An investigation into {name} has found something. It is waiting for your approval in the Heat tab.

Heat.WindowsHint: Open from the moment a gig outcome is reported until its effect shows on the price. Trades placed inside are checked once it closes and any orders placed in it have filled.
Heat.AwaitingFills: closed, waiting for orders to fill

TierHint.noticed: 25-49. Their broker sends a nervous warning.
TierHint.flagged: 50-74. NCPD sends an enquiry, and broker orders are a day slower and cost half as much again.
TierHint.investigated: 75 and up. A penalty is chosen: a fine, a frozen account, or a broker who walks away.

Panel.Title: Cover your tracks
Panel.Intro: People have noticed how you trade. You can try to make it go away, but each try takes a skill roll and costs money whether it works or not, and cannot be repeated for a while. A bribe that is refused makes things worse.
Panel.Frozen: Your account is frozen until day {until}. You cannot trade or withdraw until then, but you can still pay money in.
Panel.BrokerBan: Your old broker will not take you back until day {until}.

Result.critical: {action}: a perfect job. The trail goes cold. ({total} against DV {dv}; {cost} spent.)
Result.success: {action}: it works. Things should quiet down. ({total} against DV {dv}; {cost} spent.)
Result.failure: {action}: it does not take. Nothing changes. ({total} against DV {dv}; {cost} spent.)
Result.fumble: {action}: it goes badly, and people will have noticed. ({total} against DV {dv}; {cost} spent.)

mask.Name: Mask the pattern
mask.Desc: Run offsetting trades so the pattern is harder to read. Cheap, and you can do it often, but it only takes a little off.

books.Name: Cook the books
books.Desc: Make the paperwork tell a different story. A solid reduction for a modest price.

front.Name: Front company
front.Desc: Route your trades through a front. Takes a little off now, and halves the heat from any new audit for a week.

bribe.Name: Pay someone off
bribe.Desc: Put eddies in the right pocket. Takes the most off, but it is dear, hard to pull off, and a refusal gets talked about.

Tools.Title: Tools
Tools.Schema: Stored data is on schema v{version}.
Tools.CheckHint: Looks over companies, funds, the market, portfolios and the Night City Messenger link for anything broken or odd. Nothing is changed.
Tools.MacrosHint: Creates macros for opening the terminal and console, advancing the market a day and running the self-check. Foundry only lets Trusted players and above run script macros, so players can also use the button in the scene controls. Macros that already exist are left alone.
Tools.SuggestHint: Organisations named on Night City Messenger contacts and on gigs that are not companies on this market yet. Create one to open the company editor with the name filled in, or ignore it (gigs for an ignored client move no price).
Tools.TradeLogHint: The latest fills across every portfolio. Each portfolio only keeps its last 40 closed orders, so older ones drop off.

Verify.SummaryWarn: Self-check found {warn} warning(s). See the Tools tab or the console.
Verify.SummaryFail: Self-check found {fail} problem(s) and {warn} warning(s). See the Tools tab or the console.

Clock.RolledBack: The calendar went back, so the market went back with it, to tick {tick}. Ticking resumes as the date moves forward again.
Clock.RolledBackAhead: The calendar went back. The market rolled back {n} tick(s) but could go no further, so it is still {ahead} day(s) ahead of the calendar and will wait for the date to catch up.
Clock.Ahead: The calendar went back, but the market could not be rolled back (the ticks were too old, or players' money has moved). It is {ahead} day(s) ahead and will wait for the date to catch up.

Migration.Failed: Night City Investments could not update its stored data to schema v{version}. See the console. Nothing has been lost.

Keybindings.OpenTerminalHint: Not bound by default. Choose a key to open the market from anywhere.
Keybindings.OpenConsoleHint: GM only. Not bound by default.
Keybindings.OpenBusinessHint: Not bound by default. Opens the window where players run their businesses.

Voice.Label: Voice
Voice.Hint: Brokers with a character sheet write in the voice of the Personality on it. Others use the standard wording.

Log.glide: {company} glide scripted from {from} to {to} over {days} days
Log.gig: Gig outcome on {company}: {percent}%, showing in {days} day(s)
Log.undo: Undid tick {from}; the market is back at tick {to}

Preview.Title: Preview: {title} ({days} days ahead)
Preview.SummarySingle: Typical result (median): {median}, against {base} without it. Nine times in ten it lands between {low} and {high}. In {higher}% of {paths} simulated futures it ends higher than it would have without the change.
Preview.SummaryGroup: The average of the companies affected: {median} (median), against {base} without it. Nine times in ten between {low} and {high}. Higher than without the change in {higher}% of {paths} futures.
Preview.Note: The shaded bands are the middle 80% of simulated futures. They use their own random numbers, so this shows what is likely, not what will happen.

Reason.not-active-gm: Only the active GM can run a preview.
Reason.no-market: The market has not started yet.
Reason.no-targets: That target has no companies in it.
Reason.glide-too-steep: That glide asks for too big a move per day. Give it more days or a closer target.

Glide.Title: Scripted glide
Glide.Hint: Steer one company toward a target price over a number of days, landing on it exactly on the last day. Noise is how much of the usual day-to-day movement is kept on the way. Fair value follows, so the price does not snap back afterwards.
Glide.Started: Glide scheduled. It starts on the next tick.

Ipo.Title: Upcoming IPOs
Ipo.SubscribeHint: Shares are offered at {price} eb each. Your money is held, not spent, until the company lists. If the offer is oversubscribed you may receive fewer shares.
Ipo.ListNowConfirm: List {name} on the market now and fill every subscription?
Ipo.EditorHint: To launch a company later, untick Listed above and set a date. It lists on that in-world date. Leave the date empty for no IPO.

SettlementDays.Name: Sale settlement delay (days)
SettlementDays.Hint: How long the proceeds of a sale take to become spendable. 0 is at once. While settling they count towards a portfolio's value but cannot be spent or withdrawn.

ShowTicker.Name: Show the market ticker strip
ShowTicker.Hint: A small strip at the top of the screen with the NC index and either the companies you have starred (up to four) or, if you have none, the day's biggest movers. Click it to open the Market Terminal. This setting is only for you.

TickMode.Name: Market tick mode
TickMode.Hint: How the market advances. In-world clock: one tick every set number of minutes of Simple Calendar time (below). If the calendar jumps forward the market catches up a game day at a time; if it goes back, the market just takes the new date. In-world day: one tick per day the calendar moves forward, and the market rolls back if the date is rolled back. Manual: only when the GM advances it.

RealTimeMinutes.Name: Tick interval (in-world minutes)
RealTimeMinutes.Hint: Only used when the tick mode is the in-world clock. One tick for every this many minutes of Simple Calendar time (24 hours of 60 minutes), however fast the clock runs. Anything that lasts days (a gig's delay, a sentiment change, a heat window, a broker's speed) is counted in game days, so this only sets how finely prices move.

GigImpactApproval.Name: GM approves gig impacts
GigImpactApproval.Hint: When on, market impacts from Night City Map gig outcomes wait for GM approval in the Gigs tab. When off they are applied automatically (a client that needs mapping, or only a close match, still waits).

GigImpacts.Name: Gig outcomes move the market
GigImpacts.Hint: Needs the Night City Map bridge module. When off, completed and failed gigs are ignored.

GigImpactScale.Name: Gig impact strength
GigImpactScale.Hint: Scales every gig impact. 1 is normal: a 1,000 eb job moves its client by about 1.5%, and a failure by more.

HeatEnabled.Name: Track insider-trading heat
HeatEnabled.Hint: Watch for trades on a gig's client in the gap before its effect shows on the price, and record a hidden heat score for each character (see the Heat tab). What the heat does to players is set by the next two settings.

HeatConsequences.Name: Warn and penalise suspicious trading
HeatConsequences.Hint: When on, rising heat has consequences: a warning from the player's broker, an enquiry from NCPD, slower and dearer broker orders while flagged, and at the top a penalty. It also lets warned players try to cover their tracks. When off, heat is only recorded.

HeatPenaltyApproval.Name: GM approves penalties
HeatPenaltyApproval.Hint: When on (the default), a fine, account freeze or dropped broker waits in the Heat tab for you to approve, change or dismiss. When off, penalties are carried out as soon as they are found. Warnings and enquiries are always sent.

HeatStrength.Name: Heat strength
HeatStrength.Hint: Scales how much heat each suspicious trade adds. 1 is normal: a medium trade (about 3,000 eb) is worth around 14 heat, two or three of them reach the first warning bracket, and larger trades draw more.

GigTips.Name: Mail rumours before a gig shows in the price
GigTips.Hint: Players who hold or watch the client and have turned on "Rumours" get a vague mail from their broker before the effect lands.

BrokerOrderMode.Name: Broker order handling
BrokerOrderMode.Hint: Auto: orders mailed to a broker are processed automatically after the broker's delay. Manual: each order waits in the GM queue.

DepositFee.Name: Deposit fee (eb)
DepositFee.Hint: Flat fee charged when a player deposits funds into their brokerage balance.

DirectExecution.Name: Direct order execution
DirectExecution.Hint: Only used when direct trading access is Open: when a player trades directly, fill at the next market tick or immediately at the current quote.

DirectCommission.Name: Direct trading commission (basis points)
DirectCommission.Hint: Commission on direct terminal trades, the most expensive way to trade. 100 basis points is 1%. Broker fees are always a share of this, set by the broker's Accounting skill.

DirectMode.Name: Direct trading access
DirectMode.Hint: Terminal: direct trades need a CorpNet terminal and a passed Accounting check. Open: anyone can trade directly with no check (the older behaviour).

DirectFlatFee.Name: Direct trading flat fee (eb)
DirectFlatFee.Hint: Charged on every direct trade. Brokers charge a lower share of this.

CorpnetDV.Name: Terminal check DV
CorpnetDV.Hint: The Accounting check a character must beat (INT + Accounting + 1d10) to open a direct trading session.

CorpnetNetwork.Name: Terminal network
CorpnetNetwork.Hint: The Night City Messenger network a device must be connected to for direct trading. Use the network's id, for example CORPNET.

SessionTicks.Name: Session length (market days)
SessionTicks.Hint: How many market days a passed check keeps direct trading open.

LockoutTicks.Name: Lockout after a failed check (market days)
LockoutTicks.Hint: How long a character is locked out after failing the check. A fumble doubles it.

DebugMode.Name: Debug logging
DebugMode.Hint: Write extra diagnostics to the browser console.

BusinessesEnabled.Name: Player businesses
BusinessesEnabled.Hint: Let players found and run their own businesses, with the Business window. Turning this off stops their weeks closing and refuses new requests; nothing is deleted.

BusinessApproval.Name: New businesses need GM approval
BusinessApproval.Hint: A business that has passed its setup roll and has its money waits in the GM Console's Businesses tab until the GM lets it open.

SyndicatesEnabled.Name: Player syndicates
SyndicatesEnabled.Hint: Let players pool money in a syndicate that trades on the market as one account. Turning this off refuses new syndicate requests; existing syndicates keep their holdings and nothing is deleted.

SyndicateMail.Name: Mail syndicate members
SyndicateMail.Hint: Send members a Night City Messenger mail from the market wire when a proposal opens and when it passes, fails or lapses, when an agreed payment fails, when their redemption is paid, and when the syndicate is wound up.

SyndicateApproval.Name: New syndicates need GM approval
SyndicateApproval.Hint: A syndicate a player founds waits in the GM Console's Syndicates tab until the GM approves it. Until then no money can be paid in.

BusinessWeekday.Name: Business week ends on
BusinessWeekday.Hint: Every business's operating week closes on the first market tick on or after this day. The day of your weekly session works well.

BusinessGrowthRate.Name: Business growth rate
BusinessGrowthRate.Hint: Scales how fast businesses build Reputation and Capacity. 1 is the calibrated pace; 1.5 suits a campaign that wants players' businesses to grow sooner.

Proposed.Subject: New proposal to vote on
Proposed.Body: Proposed by {name}. Vote in the market terminal's Portfolio tab, with the syndicate picked, before {date}.

Passed.Subject: Proposal passed
Passed.Body: Members holding more than half the units agreed.

Failed.Subject: Proposal turned down
Failed.Body: Members holding half the units or more said no.

Lapsed.Subject: Proposal lapsed
Lapsed.Body: Not enough members agreed before the vote closed.

Void.Subject: Proposal passed but could not be carried out

AgreedFailed.Subject: An agreed payment or trade failed
AgreedFailed.Body: The members agreed it, but it could not be done: {reason}.

Redeemed.Subject: Redemption paid
Redeemed.Body: {units} units of {name} were redeemed for {amount} eb, paid into your brokerage balance.

Dissolved.Subject: Syndicate wound up
Dissolved.Body: The syndicate has been dissolved. Its cash was paid into the members' brokerage balances by units.

Charter.Gains: Chartering makes the business a company: three action slots a week, a Capacity ceiling of 14, shares in place of units, and later monthly reports and officers. Rent, licences and actions (DV 17) cost more. It takes every partner's agreement, naming the ticker, then three rolls any partner can make: the business plan, the registration and the capital structure. The 2,000 eb filing fee is paid when you agree, whatever happens.
Charter.SectorLine: As a company it would be in the {sector} sector.
Charter.Range: Its capital quote will be between {min} and {max} eb, depending on the capital structure roll; the business's net assets count toward it.
Charter.Confirm: Propose chartering the business? If every partner agrees, the 2,000 eb filing fee is paid from its cash at once, and the three charter rolls open.
Charter.Agreed: The partners have agreed to charter as {ticker}. Any partner may make each roll.
Charter.Awaiting: Waiting for the GM: a capital quote of {quote} eb, of which the business's net assets cover {assets} eb, leaving {shortfall} eb to pay in.
Charter.Funding: The GM has approved the charter. Pay in {shortfall} eb by {date} ({paid} eb so far, at most {max} eb): each payment buys shares at book value. The company is formed when it is met.
Charter.Refused: The capital structure roll failed, so the charter was refused. You can agree to try again from {date}.
Charter.Rejected: The GM turned the charter down; anything paid in was refunded.
Charter.Lapsed: The funding window ran out; everything paid in was refunded.
Charter.Kept: Kept for the next try (30 days): {parts}.

GMSyndicate.Title: Player syndicates
GMSyndicate.Intro: Each syndicate's members, its account and what is waiting. You can pass or veto any proposal, and close a syndicate whose account holds nothing but cash (it is paid out by units).
GMSyndicate.Disabled: Player syndicates are switched off in the module settings. Existing syndicates keep their holdings.
GMSyndicate.RejectConfirm: Turn this syndicate down? Nothing has been paid in yet, so it is simply removed.
GMSyndicate.CloseConfirm: Close this syndicate? Its cash is paid into the members' brokerage balances by units, and it stops trading.
GMSyndicate.CloseLater: To close it, its account must first hold nothing but cash.
GMSyndicate.Money: Cash {cash} eb · value {total} eb · {nav} eb a unit · officers' limit {limit} eb a day each

GMBusiness.CharterRejectConfirm: Turn this charter down? Anything the partners paid in is refunded; the filing fee is not.

Charter.awaiting: Charter as {ticker} waiting for you: {rolls}. Quote {quote} eb, net assets {assets} eb, shortfall {shortfall} eb.
Charter.funding: Charter as {ticker} approved: {shortfall} eb to be paid in by {date}.

GMBusiness.Title: Player businesses
GMBusiness.Intro: Every business at every stage, with its true state, Exposure included. Players see their own businesses only, as bands rather than numbers.
GMBusiness.NoneWaiting: No business is waiting for approval.
GMBusiness.RejectConfirm: Turn this business down? Every partner gets their share of the money back.
GMBusiness.LeavesHint: For a character who has died or left the table: the buy-out rule applies to their stake.
GMBusiness.RemoveConfirm: Delete this business's record for good? No money moves.
GMBusiness.SetupFailed: Setup roll {band}: can be tried again (range {range}).
GMBusiness.Week: Week {n} closes on or after {end}; slots used: {used}.

shakedown.Name: A shakedown
shakedown.Hint: A gang wants protection money on top of what you already pay.

theft.Name: A break-in
theft.Hint: Someone has been through the stock overnight, and they will be back.

breakdown.Name: Something breaks
breakdown.Hint: The kit the business runs on has given out.

shortage.Name: A supply shortage
shortage.Hint: The usual supplier cannot deliver this week.

rival.Name: A rival opens nearby
rival.Hint: A competitor is undercutting you and talking you down.

collectors.Name: Debt collectors
collectors.Hint: The fixer wants the payment you missed, and has sent people to make the point.

trouble.Name: Trouble with a customer
trouble.Hint: A customer, or a job, has gone wrong in a way people will talk about.

inspection.Name: An inspection
inspection.Hint: The city's inspectors want to see the books and the licences.

windfall.Name: A big order
windfall.Hint: Someone with money wants something done this week, if you can deliver.

Syndicate.Title: Syndicate: {name}
Syndicate.LimitText: Each officer can trade, and put into businesses, up to {amount} eb a game day without a vote. Anything bigger, and every other decision, goes to the members, who vote by units for up to {days} days.
Syndicate.LimitLeft: You have {left} eb of today's limit left.
Syndicate.LeaveConfirm: Leaving redeems all your units at the value per unit on the day they are paid, after the market's settlement delay, and then takes you off the members' list. Leave the syndicate?
Syndicate.MoneyHint: Paying in moves eddies from your own brokerage balance and buys units at today's value per unit. Redeeming sells units back at the value on the day they are paid, after the market's settlement delay, into your brokerage balance; it waits while the syndicate is short of cash.

role.member: Make {name} a member again, no longer an officer

Proposal.limit: Set the officers' limit to {amount} eb an order

business.buyout: Buy a stake in {name} for about {amount} eb

Proposal.dissolve: Dissolve the syndicate and pay out its cash by units

VoteSent.yes: Your yes vote has been sent.
VoteSent.no: Your no vote has been sent.

Syndicate.ProposeHint: A proposal passes when members holding more than half the units say yes; it fails when half or more say no, and lapses at the end of its voting period. To dissolve, the officers first sell every holding.
Syndicate.RedemptionLine: {name}: {units} units, paid from {date} if the cash is there

Ledger.tradeFailed: The members agreed a trade, but it could not be placed: {text} ({reason})
Ledger.businessFailed: The members agreed to put money into {business}, but it could not be done: {reason}

Syndicate.Heading: Syndicates
Syndicate.Intro: Shared brokerage accounts. Members pay in from their own brokerage balances and hold units in one, officers trade it, and bigger decisions go to a vote. Click a syndicate to open its account.
Syndicate.FoundHint: You will be its first officer. The characters you invite can join or decline.
Syndicate.TradeNote: This order is for the syndicate. You have {left} eb of your {amount} eb daily limit left; a bigger order is sent to the members as a proposal instead.
Syndicate.NotOfficer: Only the syndicate's officers can trade its account. Ask an officer, or propose the trade to the members.

Done.found: Syndicate founded. If the GM approves new syndicates, it waits for them first.
Done.leave: You are leaving the syndicate: your units will be redeemed.

Reason.bad-name: the name needs at least two characters
Reason.no-id: the syndicate could not be created
Reason.not-active: the syndicate is waiting for the GM's approval
Reason.bad-amount: that is not a valid amount
Reason.no-portfolio: you have no brokerage account yet
Reason.insufficient-cash: not enough free cash in your brokerage account
Reason.not-enough-units: you do not have that many units free to redeem
Reason.dissolve-instead: you are the last holder; propose dissolving the syndicate instead
Reason.no-value: the syndicate is worth nothing at the moment, so no units can be bought
Reason.bad-request: that is not something a syndicate can do
Reason.over-limit: the order is over the officers' limit; propose it to the members
Reason.too-many-proposals: too many proposals are open; vote on those first
Reason.bad-member: that character cannot be chosen for this
Reason.already-member: that character is already a member or invited
Reason.not-liquid: the account still holds shares, open orders or money settling; sell first
Reason.already-proposed: the same proposal is already open
Reason.no-proposal: that proposal is no longer open
Reason.not-pending: the syndicate is not waiting for approval
Reason.disabled: the GM has switched syndicates off
Reason.error: something went wrong; the GM can see the details in the console

Business.Title: Business
Business.StartHint: Found another business with this character.
Business.Disabled: Player businesses are turned off in the module settings.
Business.NoCharacter: You have no character to run a business with.
Business.StartIntro: A side business needs no charter: a stall, a garage bay, a back-room clinic. Put in what eddies and gear you have, invite any partners, and once everyone has answered, any partner makes the setup roll.
Business.Name: Name
Business.LocationHint: e.g. a back room in Watson
Business.GearDrop: Gear you bring (optional): drag an item here from your character's sheet, the Items directory or a compendium. Its book value is its market price.
Business.GearLeaves: leaves your sheet; back if the business never opens
Business.SweatHint: An optional slice of units for the partner who will do most of the work. Decisions follow units; closing the business, and changing the agreement, need every partner.
Business.ReadOnly: You are a member of this syndicate, not an officer: you can see its businesses, but only its officers act for it.
Business.SyndicateCashOnly: A syndicate puts in cash only. Its officers can bring gear as partners in their own right.
Business.ProposedToSyndicate: That is over {name}'s officers' limit, so the {amount} eb has gone to its members as a proposal. It is paid in once they agree.
Business.InvitationIntro: You have been asked to be a partner in {name}. Put in what you like; your units follow what you put in.
Business.AwaitingGM: Everything is ready. The GM has to approve the business before it opens.
Business.Escrow: Money in, held until it opens
Business.SetupIntro: The setup roll sets how much of the setup cost the business needs and the Capacity it opens with.
Business.SetupPassed: Setup roll: {band}. It needs {cost} eb of setup (gear counts) and opens at Capacity {capacity}.
Business.SetupFailed: Setup roll: {band}. You can try again from {date}.
Business.Shortfall: {amount} eb more is needed before it can open.
Business.TopUpHint: Eddies go into the business's cash and gear into the fit-out. Nobody's units change, so every holder's stake gains in proportion; you are not given a bigger share for it.
Business.WithdrawConfirm: Take your share of the money back out and leave the business before it opens?
Business.WeekRuns: This operating week runs from {from} and closes at the first market tick on or after {to} ({day}).
Business.HelpHint: A complementary check: no slot, and on a success the partner who takes this action gets +1. One check a week each.
Business.AlreadyHelped: This character has already made a complementary check this week.
Business.UnworkedNote: A week nobody works the shop still trades, at a little under the usual takings. Reputation drifts back toward the district's usual and costs creep up when nobody looks after them.

work.Name: Work the shop
work.Hint: With the trade's skills: sets the week's takings.

promote.Name: Promote
promote.Hint: Persuasion, Wardrobe & Style, Composition, Credibility or Charismatic Impact: Reputation and foot traffic up.

source.Name: Source supplies
source.Hint: Trading, Streetwise or Operator: the Cost base down.

fixUp.Name: Fix the place up
fixUp.Hint: Basic Tech or Maker: Capacity up, so more takings are possible.

keepSafe.Name: Keep it safe
keepSafe.Hint: Tactics, Persuasion, Combat Awareness or Backup: less protection money this week.

Business.DrawAllowance: You may draw up to {amount} eb: your share of last week's profit.
Business.NoDraw: Nothing to draw: draws come from last week's profit, split by units, once a week.
Business.NoHistory: The charts fill in as each week closes.

Ledger.foundedGear: Founded by {name}, who also brought {gear} eb of gear
Ledger.contributionGear: {name} put in money and {gear} eb of gear
Ledger.liquidation: Closed: paid out to the partners ({salvage} eb from the gear)
Ledger.charterRefused: Charter refused: the capital structure roll failed
Ledger.gigDone: A gig for the business went well
Ledger.gigFailed: A gig for the business went wrong

Business.PutIn: put in {cash} eb and {gear} eb of gear
Business.LeavingSince: Leaving: the others may buy the stake at book value until {date}.

Agreement.decision: Day-to-day decisions by majority of units; closing the business needs every partner.
Agreement.buyout: When a partner leaves or dies, the others may buy their stake at book value within {days} days. Otherwise it passes to their named heir, without a vote, or lapses.

Business.HeirHint: Who gets your units, without a vote but with draws, if the others do not buy them when you leave.
Business.CloseConfirm: Propose closing the business? If every partner agrees, the gear is sold for half its value and everything is paid out by units.
Business.LeaveConfirm: Offer your stake to your partners? They have the buy-out window to buy it at book value; after that it goes to your heir.
Business.DecisionsHint: Closing needs every partner with a vote; one refusal ends the proposal.
Business.DaysLeft: You have {n} business day(s) left this week.
Business.WaitingVote: {n} proposal(s) waiting for votes on the Partners tab.
Business.ProjectsIntro: An expansion (a second chair, a bigger bay) is paid from the business's cash when the partners agree, then finished with business days: each partner with a vote has 3 a week, and days not spent lapse when the week closes.
Business.ProjectProgress: Expansion under way since {date}: {days} of {need} business days done. When finished, Capacity rises by {gain}.
Business.ExpansionOffer: An expansion here costs {cost} eb from the business's cash and {days} business days of work, and raises Capacity by {gain}. Starting one needs a majority of the voting units.
Business.ExpansionPending: An expansion is waiting for the partners' votes.
Business.NextStageLater: Chartering a company comes in a later version of the module. A registered business can stay as it is for good.

Milestone.profit: Average weekly profit of {need} eb over the last 4 weeks
Milestone.fee: {need} eb of the business's cash for the registration fee
Milestone.charterProfit: Average weekly profit of {need} eb over the last 4 weeks
Milestone.charterFee: {need} eb of the business's cash for the filing fee

Business.RegisterGains: Registering means two action slots a week and lower protection money, but rent and licence fees go up, actions are rolled at DV 15, and the business has a Compliance standing to look after. It takes every partner's agreement, then a registration roll: Bureaucracy, or Local Expert or Persuasion at DV +2. The fee is paid whatever the result.
Business.StepUpPending: Stepping up is waiting for every partner's vote.
Business.StepUpAgreed: The partners have agreed to register. Any partner may make the registration roll.
Business.StepUpRetry: The last registration was refused; it can be tried again from {date}.
Business.StepUpConfirm: Propose registering the business? Every partner has to agree.

Rule.majority: Needs a majority of units; lapses after {date}.

Closed.failed: It went under on {date}: its cash stayed below zero for two weeks.
Closed.cancelled: It never opened: everyone took their money back ({date}).
Closed.rejected: The GM turned it down on {date}; the money went back.

capacity.full: as big as it can get here

Loan.fixer: A fixer's loan: {balance} eb owed at {rate}% a week, {payment} eb of it repaid each week.
Loan.bank: A bank loan: {balance} eb owed at {rate}% a week, {payment} eb of it repaid each week.

Business.FixerTerms: A fixer lends up to {limit} eb with no questions asked, at {rate}% a week, repaid over {weeks} weeks. A missed payment costs a late fee and Reputation, and the fixer's collectors come calling. It needs a majority of the voting units.
Business.BankTerms: A bank lends to a registered business after an Accounting or Business roll at DV 15: the better the roll, the more (6 to 20 weeks of average profit, now {profit} eb a week) and the cheaper. A missed payment costs Compliance. It needs a majority of the voting units, then any partner rolls.
Business.BankLater: Banks only lend to registered businesses.
Business.BankRetry: The bank said no; it will listen again from {date}.
Business.BankRoll: Make the case to the bank
Business.LoanPending: A loan is waiting for the partners' votes on the Partners tab.
Business.InvestorsLater: Investors only buy into registered businesses.
Business.InvestOffer: The partners offer you {units} units for {amount} eb, at {price} eb a unit. You would have a vote like any partner.
Business.AngelIntro: An angel is an outside backer. Once every partner agrees to look for one, you will know who you are pitching to; any partner then rolls Persuasion or Trading against the angel's skill. The better the pitch, the more they put in and the better the price. An angel takes units without a vote, and is paid out like any holder if the business closes.
Business.AngelRetry: The last angel walked away; another will listen from {date}.
Business.SecurityNote: A successful Keep it safe this week also deals with it.
Business.EventIfNot: Unanswered, it costs 15% of the week's takings and leaves a mark.
Business.WindfallIfNot: Unanswered, the chance simply goes by.

EventOutcome.covered: {event}: Keep it safe dealt with it.
EventOutcome.fumbled: {event}: the answer made it worse ({change} eb).

Done.found: Business founded. Your partners can now join.
Done.withdraw: You have taken your money back out.
Done.leave: Your stake is on offer to your partners.
Done.loanRoll: Your case to the bank is recorded.
